Many gamers have complained regarding the same from the past year, yet without any resolution. This shows how much dedicated IOI is towards their user base.

Thirdly, while purchasing Hitman 3 you will get confused on which packs to buy as IOI has made a mess out of it with very little to no information regarding the packs on their Steam store page.

Deceptive Marketing – Don’t Be Fooled!

I’m honestly so frustrated with how this game is marketed. "World of Assassination – Part 1" goes on sale all the time, and everything about it the title, icon, even the store page makes it look like you're getting the full game. The only way you can tell you’re not getting the whole thing is if you scroll all the way down to some tiny details.
After buying it, I realized I only got about 30% of the game, with the rest locked behind DLCs. This isn’t just bad practice; it feels like a straight-up bait-and-switch to get you to buy more after you’ve already paid.
DLC isn’t the issue, but how they hide it is. If you’re thinking of getting this, just know you’re not getting the full game.

The third and final part to the Hitman trilogy. If you liked this first two, this is a must-have purchase. In my opinion, the series is one of the greatest in gaming history. The Hitman games have always allowed players to control the experience and get what they want out of it. Want to run around and shoot everyone in sight while taking return gunfire? You can. Want to stealthily take out your targets only in creative ways? You can. Want a 007-esque experience? You can. It's loaded with humour, hit-related puzzles, time-based routines to learn, exotic environments, cool gear and weapons, perfect sound design and flawless controls. The only element missing is the darker vibes of the older games like Silent Assassin and Blood Money.

In the future, I'd love to see a return to it or a mix of the old and new styles per level. My one issue with the game is it being online only. I understand why but it's still problematic and unfair to the customers who didn't download a cracked version and I'd strongly recommend that IO discontinues with this in the future. Overall, it's a modern classic and a must-have for anyone with taste. Thank you for the games and the memories IO Interactive, I'm looking forward to your upcoming 007 project.

The finale of the World of Assassin trilogy, Hitman 3, culminates the Hitman reboot series in a pretty sensational way. Stories in Hitman 3 are much more emotional than those in the previous installs: the decease of Grey, the revenge of 47, the fake betrayal of Diana, and the lose-all ending of Edwards. Music design is also more influential than before. Seemingly, Hitman 3 has fewer mission stories than previous episodes. However, many of Hitman 3's challenges are in fact just like puzzle-solving and clue-finding games -- they are mission stories without guides. I love this series so much. I'm hooked to them. Looking forward to the new updates and IOI's new 007 game!

HITMAN World of Assassination bundles HITMAN 1, 2, and 3 into one game. It's a little annoying, since I purchased the original and sequel as seperate packages, but those who haven't played any of the titles will benefit from one price and title.

A stealth, action, open world, adventure, and sandbox all in one, this iteration of HITMAN is a game I'm very fond of. Each map feels immersive, with numerous ways to take out each target - thus there is a good level of replayability. Civilian NPCs do a reasonable job of keeping the world alive, whilst enemy NPCs are generally responsive to you being seen or your actions.

A good looking game with a neat soundtrack, HITMAN is a game I would recommend to just about anyone.

I own every Hitman game and I'm a huge fan. Although purchasing everything was pretty confusing, it looks like this has been simplified now. That's great! The games and the world of Hitman is fantastic and the new Freelancer mode is what I've been wishing for, for this game since the beginning. I also have absolutely no idea why people are whining about it. It's free, FREE! I would have easily paid $10 for it and so I'm about to pick up the two new DLC packs to show some more support. One minor confusion is that the store is showing that I don't own the 7 Deadly Sins pack, although I previously purchased it. I checked and it's showing in the game though.

This game is the expected extension to the HITMAN series, and keeps the mechanics from the new era HITMAN 1 and HITMAN 2. I like the story, the gameplay, the engine and quality of these games. I especially like how good it looks even on lower-end hardware like the RX 580.

But, purchasing, transferring data and even starting as a new player in this "World of Assassination" is unnecessarily confusing. Not only is it hard to understand the "editions" and DLC, even if you get exactly what you're looking for, you need to transfer old account data using a website link. When you do this transfer, it doesn't get all your data in from last games like we saw with HITMAN 2 release. Instead, I felt as if 30-40% of my progression/achievements were lost. Even now after purchasing and playing, I still don't quite understand all the modes, what requires payments or why, or exactly what content you will get for the money. It's just flat out hard to understand.

Positive reviews remain for HITMAN 1 and HITMAN 2, but this edition, apparently the last to the HITMAN "new era" franchise has just annoyed me.

A masterful puzzle stealth game with top-tier level crafting. The near-infinite replayability with a well-executed set of mechanics make this game one of a kind.

Only 2 things wrong with the game:
- Colorado. (Note: This is a joke, but it indeed is my least favorite map in the main game.)
- IOI obfuscating the steam store page to confuse people into buying the wrong thing. To play the full game, get at least the standard one ("HITMAN World of Assassination" as of writing this review), or get the Deluxe Version . The Deluxe Pack contains the Seven Deadly Sins DLC, which has been quite negatively received by the community.

For people looking into speed-running the game: The always-online requirements can be mitigated if you use an IOI server emulator (such as Peacock). (This also removes part of the grind for mastery levels, and has support for auto-split-times.)

This is the best game ever! But I would recommend peacock project (custom server) and Simple Mod Framework for a better experience. Trust me, its worth it. The main game is still really fun and I would recommend buying it (With a steam key)

I really enjoyed this game. The gameplay feels pretty immersive and the levels have a lot of replayability. Lots of time put into environment design, NPC behavior, and interactions. It's great that it is that way since you really only have access to like a handful of levels.
The reason I wouldn't recommend the game though is because the way it advertises itself seems very predatory. Very confusing on what you're actually buying and how to buy follow-up content. In fact, it seems like a lot of the investments into the UI is buying and managing all the DLC's you can get. You can see the content from Hitman 2, 3, etc but hit with the paid access screen. You can see all the other modes as well that are behind another paywall.
I guess in a way the base version is a cheap demo? Which is fine... though when I buy a game I'd rather it be contained and without advertisements even if it's just self-advertising additional content. Also, paid DLC's SHOULD NOT encompass >60% of the game content.

An imaginative masterpiece indeed, looking forward to the next generation (if there will be).

You release the game as Epic exclusive - a store that is still lacking user features and you do that despite all the previous entries in reboot series being on Steam, finally after a year you drop it on Steam, making a mess of a purchase page instead of using depots. Then decide to "simplify it" but what you mean in the process is you remove the ability to have content from 2 previous entries automatically added to Hitman 3, now forcing people that want to replay those levels to purchase that content yet again at an extremely high price, while having useful idiots insult anyone who criticises your anti-consumer, bad decisions... so I am going to do what Epic Games stores doesn't allow you to do - leave you a bad "review".

Oh yeah and almost forgot - this will be almost entirely unplayable without server emulator, when IOI decides that the game doesn't sell anymore and shuts downs its servers.

What is there to say about Hitman 3? The large maps and sandbox nature are key to the experience and something I strongly recommend for players who want to have the ability to craft nonsensical assassination plots. 47's deadpan humor is unmatched and the voice cast is stellar. I purchased this game and all of its content as a result of binge watching Hitman content from the Oxbox crew. Overall, I strongly recommend the game, though I caution that it is really only worth it if you have the previous two games or you can splurge for the addition of the full series's content. Therefore, given the expenditure for getting said content, I would say that anyone who is only tentatively interested in the game should wait for it going on sale.
